- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward adjustment by 1–2 periods.  
- In high-sentiment environments, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; apply a 5–10% downward bias to forecasted mean.  
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > true by >5%), apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce next period’s forecast by 5–10% to avoid momentum overhang.  
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.5) and forecast diverges from history, favor historical trend alignment over sentiment-driven extrapolation.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–3% for each period where sentiment is neutral or negative.
